allFormulas.summary: A simple two-ingredient topical powder made from Pearl and Cattle Gallstone (Bezoar), traditionally blown onto the throat or applied to mouth sores. It clears Heat-toxin and promotes tissue healing, making it useful for sore throats, tonsillitis, oral ulcers that won't heal, and gum inflammation.
categories: Topical formulas for sores and wounds
tcmActions: Promotes tissue regeneration and heals sores

allFormulas.name: Xi Huang Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from Qing Dynasty surgical medicine, designed to clear toxic Heat, dissolve stubborn nodules, and improve Blood circulation. It is traditionally used for hard breast lumps, swollen lymph nodes, deep abscesses, and various types of masses. In modern practice, it is widely used as adjunctive support alongside conventional cancer treatment, particularly for breast, liver, and lung cancers, as well as for benign breast hyperplasia and lymphadenitis.
tcmActions: Dispels Blood stasis and stops pain
otherNames: Xi Huang Wan (西黄丸)

allFormulas.name: Gan Cao Fu Zi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Shang Han Lun used to relieve severe joint pain, stiffness, and swelling caused by Wind, Cold, and Dampness penetrating the joints when the body's warming and protective functions are weakened. It warms the channels, disperses Cold, and eliminates Dampness from the joints.
tcmActions: Warms the channels and disperses Cold
Strengthens the Spleen to resolve Dampness
allFormulas.dynasty: Eastern Han dynasty (东汉), circa 200 CE
otherNames: Si Wu Fu Zi Tang (四物附子汤, Four-Substance Aconite Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Bai Hu Jia Gui Zhi Tang
allFormulas.englishName: White Tiger Plus Cinnamon Twig Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for joint inflammation with strong internal Heat. It combines powerful fever-reducing and fluid-replenishing herbs with Cinnamon Twig (Gui Zhi) to open the channels and relieve joint pain. Originally used for a type of malaria with predominantly hot symptoms and aching bones, it is now widely applied for conditions like acute gout, rheumatic fever, and inflammatory arthritis when joints are red, hot, swollen, and painful alongside fever, thirst, and sweating.
tcmActions: Clears Heat from the Qi level
Harmonizes the Nutritive and Defensive levels
allFormulas.dynasty: Eastern Han dynasty (东汉), approximately 200 CE
otherNames: Gui Zhi Bai Hu Tang (桂枝白虎汤)
Zhi Mu Tang (知母汤, Anemarrhena Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Bao Yin Jian
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from Zhang Jingyue's Jing Yue Quan Shu designed for conditions where depleted Yin leads to internal Heat that causes abnormal bleeding. It is especially used for gynecological issues such as heavy menstrual periods, prolonged bleeding, uterine bleeding, and threatened miscarriage when accompanied by signs of Heat like warm palms and soles, a red tongue, and a rapid pulse. The formula works by simultaneously cooling the Blood to control bleeding and rebuilding the body's Yin reserves to address the root cause.

allFormulas.name: Bai Hu Jia Ren Shen Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for clearing intense internal Heat while replenishing Qi and body fluids. It is used when strong fever, heavy sweating, and intense thirst have left the body both overheated and depleted, as seen in high fevers, heatstroke, or conditions like diabetes with excessive thirst.
tcmActions: Clears Heat from the Qi level
allFormulas.dynasty: Eastern Han dynasty (东汉), circa 200 CE
otherNames: Ren Shen Bai Hu Tang (人参白虎汤, Ginseng and White Tiger Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Yu Lu San
allFormulas.summary: A simple but powerful cooling formula from Song Dynasty pediatric medicine, designed to quickly clear internal Heat that causes vomiting, diarrhea, fever, and irritability in children. It combines two cold mineral substances (Gypsum and Glauberite) with Licorice root to bring down high temperatures and calm the digestive system, and is also used for heatstroke with thirst and restlessness.
tcmActions: Harmonizes the Middle Burner and stops diarrhea
otherNames: Gan Lu Yin (甘露饮, Sweet Dew Drink)
Yu Lu Yin (玉露饮, Jade Dew Drink)

allFormulas.name: Qi Lin Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical fertility-support formula that nourishes the Kidneys, fills Essence, and strengthens Qi and Blood. It is used for both men and women experiencing reproductive difficulties linked to Kidney deficiency and insufficient Qi and Blood, such as low sperm quality, irregular periods, fatigue, and weak lower back.
tcmActions: Tonifies the Kidneys and fills Essence
keyIngredients: Zhi He Shou Wu (Prepared Fleeceflower Root)
allIngredients: Zhi He Shou Wu (Prepared Fleeceflower Root)
otherNames: Zhu Yun Yu Er Wan (助孕育儿丸)

allFormulas.name: Xi Lei San
allFormulas.summary: A classical topical powder used to clear Heat-Toxin from the throat and mouth, promote healing of ulcerated tissue, and relieve swelling and pain. It is applied directly to sore, ulcerated areas of the throat, mouth, or gums, and is also used as a retention enema for intestinal ulcers.
tcmActions: Removes necrotic tissue and promotes tissue regeneration
allFormulas.dynasty: Qing dynasty, no later than 1749 CE (original recording); formally named 1852 CE
otherNames: Lan Hou Sha Fang (烂喉痧方, Rotting Throat Rash Formula)
Ba Wei Xi Lei San (八味锡类散, Eight-Ingredient Tin-like Powder)

allFormulas.name: Ding Jing Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical gynecological formula from Fu Qingzhu's Gynecology designed to regulate irregular menstrual cycles. It works by soothing the Liver's free flow of Qi and nourishing the Kidney's essence, addressing the root cause when periods come sometimes early, sometimes late, with no predictable pattern.
allFormulas.dynasty: Qīng dynasty (清代), c. late 17th century

allFormulas.name: San Miao Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical three-herb formula used to clear Heat and dry Dampness from the lower body. It is commonly used for joint pain, swelling, numbness, and weakness in the legs and knees caused by Damp-Heat accumulating in the lower part of the body, including conditions like gout, lower limb arthritis, and eczema.
tcmActions: Clears Damp-Heat from the lower Jiao
Directs therapeutic action downward to the lower body
otherNames: San Miao San (三妙散, Three-Marvel Powder)

allFormulas.name: Huang Qin Hua Shi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Warm Disease school designed to clear Heat and resolve Dampness from the Middle Jiao. It is used for conditions where both internal and external Dampness combine with Heat, causing recurring low-grade fevers, body aches, a slippery tongue coating, and digestive sluggishness. The formula works by cooling the Heat component while simultaneously draining the Dampness through urination.

allFormulas.name: Wu Ji Bai Feng Wan
allFormulas.summary: A famous women's health formula used to restore Qi and Blood when both are depleted, causing irregular periods, excessive vaginal discharge, physical weakness, lower back soreness, and fatigue. Built around whole black-boned chicken combined with nearly twenty herbs, it gently tonifies without being too heavy, making it one of the most widely used tonics in Chinese medicine.
allFormulas.dynasty: Ming dynasty, 1615 CE (refined by Qing dynasty imperial physicians)
otherNames: Bai Feng Wan (白凤丸, White Phoenix Pill)

allFormulas.name: Bi Yuan Fang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Song dynasty used to open blocked nasal passages, dry Dampness, and transform Phlegm. It addresses nasal congestion with thick turbid discharge, loss of smell, and frontal headache caused by Wind and Dampness obstructing the nose and sinuses.
otherNames: Zhi Bi Yuan Fang (治鼻渊方, Treat-Sinusitis Formula)

allFormulas.name: Di Yu San
allFormulas.summary: A classical powder formula used to cool Blood-Heat, regulate Qi flow in the intestines, and stop bleeding. It is primarily used for hemorrhoidal pain and bleeding caused by Damp-Heat accumulating in the lower body, and can also be applied to intestinal bleeding with bright red blood.

allFormulas.name: Hou Po Da Huang Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from Zhang Zhongjing used to relieve severe abdominal and chest fullness caused by fluid accumulation and constipation. It works by moving stagnant Qi, purging heat, and driving out pathological fluid that has become trapped in the chest and digestive tract.
tcmActions: Purges Heat and unblocks the bowels

allFormulas.name: Dang Gui Jian Zhong Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Tangkuei Decoction to Construct the Middle
allFormulas.summary: A warming, blood-nourishing formula traditionally used for abdominal pain caused by Blood deficiency and Cold in the middle. Originally developed for postpartum recovery, it helps relieve cramping pain in the lower abdomen and back, supports weakened digestion, and rebuilds strength after blood loss or exhaustion.
tcmActions: Warms the Middle Jiao and tonifies deficiency
otherNames: Nei Bu Dang Gui Jian Zhong Tang (内补当归建中汤, Internally Supplementing Tangkuei Center-Fortifying Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Jia Jian Fu Mai Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for replenishing the body's fluids and moisture after they have been depleted by prolonged fever or illness. It addresses persistent low-grade fever, dry mouth and throat, hot palms and soles, palpitations, and irregular heartbeat caused by the loss of the body's cooling and nourishing Yin fluids. Originally created by the Qing dynasty physician Wu Jutong for the recovery stage of infectious febrile diseases.

allFormulas.name: Gui Fu Di Huang Wan
allFormulas.englishName: Cinnamon Bark and Aconite Rehmannia Pill
allFormulas.summary: A classical warming formula used to support the body when Kidney Yang (the Kidney's warming and activating function) is weakened. It addresses symptoms like persistent cold sensation in the lower back and limbs, excessive or difficult urination, swelling, fatigue, and low energy. The formula gently restores warmth by combining a rich nourishing base with small amounts of warming herbs, following the principle that sustainable warmth comes from nourishing the body's foundation rather than forceful heating.
tcmActions: Warms the lower back and knees
allFormulas.dynasty: The ancestral formula (Shen Qi Wan) dates to the Eastern Han dynasty (~200 CE). The current form with Rou Gui and Shu Di Huang evolved during the Song dynasty (~1110 CE). The name "Gui Fu Di Huang Wan" was formalized in the Qing dynasty (1742 CE).
otherNames: Ba Wei Di Huang Wan (八味地黄丸, Eight-Ingredient Rehmannia Pill)
Gui Fu Ba Wei Wan (桂附八味丸)

allFormulas.name: Xiang Su Cong Chi Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Cyperus and Perilla Decoction with Scallion and Prepared Soybean
allFormulas.summary: A gentle formula from the Revised Popular Treatise on Cold Damage, designed specifically for treating common colds during pregnancy. It combines mild Wind-Cold releasing herbs with Qi-regulating ingredients that also help calm the fetus, making it safe and effective when stronger sweating formulas would be inappropriate.
tcmActions: Releases the exterior and induces mild sweating

allFormulas.name: Qing Yan Li Ge Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Clear the Throat and Benefit the Diaphragm Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula used for severe sore throat, swollen tonsils, and throat infections caused by intense internal Heat. It works by clearing Heat and toxins from the upper body while gently purging accumulated Heat downward through the bowels, providing rapid relief for painful, swollen throat conditions with possible fever, irritability, and constipation.
tcmActions: Benefits the throat and reduces swelling
otherNames: Qing Yan Li Ge San (清咽利膈散, Clear the Throat and Benefit the Diaphragm Powder)

allFormulas.name: Zhen Ren Yang Zang Tang
allFormulas.englishName: True Man's Decoction to Nourish the Organs
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for chronic, long-standing diarrhea or dysentery that has weakened the digestive system to the point where stool slips out uncontrollably. It works by powerfully tightening the intestines to stop the leaking while warming and rebuilding the Spleen and Kidneys. Commonly used for chronic colitis, ulcerative colitis in remission, and rectal prolapse when cold-type weakness is the underlying cause.
tcmActions: Astringes the intestines and stops diarrhea
Warms and tonifies the Spleen and Kidneys
allFormulas.dynasty: Song dynasty (宋朝), first published ~1078–1151 CE
otherNames: Chún Yáng Zhēn Rén Yǎng Zàng Tāng (纯阳真人养脏汤)

allFormulas.name: Shen Xiao Gua Lou San
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula traditionally used to treat breast abscesses, mastitis, and other painful swellings caused by a buildup of Heat-toxin and blocked circulation in the tissue. It works by clearing the toxic Heat that drives the inflammation while simultaneously promoting Blood flow to relieve pain and reduce swelling. Classical texts describe it as remarkably effective for breast conditions at any stage, whether the swelling is still forming or pus has already developed.
otherNames: Si Sheng San (四圣散, Four Sages Powder)

allFormulas.name: Shi Jun Zi Wan
allFormulas.summary: A gentle classical pill formula designed primarily for children with intestinal parasites (especially roundworms) combined with poor digestion. It expels parasites while supporting the Spleen and Stomach, helping restore appetite, relieve abdominal bloating and pain, and reverse the progressive weight loss and weakness that result from parasitic infestation and nutritional decline.
tcmActions: Kills parasites and resolves gan accumulation (杀虫化疳)
Strengthens the Spleen and moves Qi (健脾行气)
allFormulas.dynasty: Song dynasty (宋代), circa 1148 CE (Shaoxing period additions)

allFormulas.name: Zi Su Zi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula originally used to treat leg weakness with breathlessness caused by turbid Qi and Phlegm rising upward while the lower body is weakened. It works by directing Qi downward, dissolving Phlegm, warming the interior, and gently supporting the lower body. It is the ancestor formula of the widely used Su Zi Jiang Qi Tang.
tcmActions: Directs Qi downward and calms wheezing
Warms the interior and disperses Cold
Warms and supports the lower body
allFormulas.dynasty: Tang dynasty, 652 CE (original Zi Su Zi Tang); Song dynasty, circa 1078-1151 CE (revised as Su Zi Jiang Qi Tang)

allFormulas.name: Hu Qian Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for weakness and wasting of the legs and lower body caused by long-term depletion of the Liver and Kidney. It works by deeply nourishing Yin, clearing deficiency Heat, and strengthening bones and sinews. It is commonly used for conditions such as osteoarthritis, osteoporosis, and other degenerative musculoskeletal disorders rooted in Yin deficiency.
otherNames: Jiàn Bù Hǔ Qián Wán (健步虎潜丸, Strengthening Gait Hidden Tiger Pill)

allFormulas.name: Gan Cao Tang
allFormulas.summary: An extremely simple one-herb classical formula from the Shang Han Lun, made only with raw licorice root. It is used for mild sore throat caused by Heat affecting the throat, gently clearing Heat and soothing inflammation. If the sore throat does not improve, a second herb (Jie Geng / Platycodon) is added to make Jie Geng Tang.
tcmActions: Soothes the throat and relieves pain
allFormulas.dynasty: Eastern Han dynasty (东汉), circa 200 CE

allFormulas.name: San Cai Tang
allFormulas.summary: A gentle three-herb formula from the Warm Disease tradition, designed to restore both Qi and body fluids after prolonged illness has left a person depleted. It is commonly used for fatigue, poor appetite, restless sleep, and dryness that persist after fevers or chronic illness, using Ginseng, Asparagus root, and Rehmannia to nourish the body from top to bottom.
allFormulas.dynasty: Qing dynasty (清朝). Yi Fang Ji Jie published 1682 CE; Wen Bing Tiao Bian completed 1798 CE. Pill form (San Cai Wan) traces to Jin dynasty, ~13th century CE.
otherNames: San Cai Wan (三才丸, Three Talents Pill)

allFormulas.name: Chai Ping Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Bupleurum and Calm the Stomach Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A classical combined formula that merges two well-known prescriptions to treat conditions where an infection or fever (lodged between the body's surface and interior) is complicated by digestive problems from excess Dampness. It addresses alternating chills and fever, nausea, bloating, poor appetite, and a heavy sensation in the body, making it especially suited for people who get sick during humid conditions or who already have a weak digestive system.

allFormulas.name: Da Ban Xia Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical three-herb formula for people who repeatedly vomit undigested food hours after eating, especially when they are weak, thin, and have dry stools. It works by restoring the Stomach's ability to move food downward while replenishing the body's depleted vitality and moisture.
categories: Formulas that harmonize the Stomach and direct rebellion downward
tcmActions: Harmonizes the Stomach and directs rebellious Qi downward

allFormulas.name: Da Xian Xiong Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Major Sinking Into the Chest Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A powerful emergency formula from the Shang Han Lun, used to treat severe conditions where water and Heat become trapped together in the chest and abdomen. It is designed for acute situations featuring intense, stone-hard abdominal pain that refuses any touch, constipation, thirst, and fever. Because of its strength, it is only used for short periods under careful supervision, and treatment is stopped as soon as the bowels open.
allFormulas.dynasty: Eastern Han dynasty (东汉), circa 200 CE
otherNames: Xian Xiong Tang (陷胸汤)

allFormulas.name: Xiao Luo Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical three-herb formula used to dissolve lumps and nodules in the neck and elsewhere in the body. It works by nourishing the body's fluids, clearing excess heat, and softening hardened masses caused by the accumulation of phlegm and fire. Commonly applied for thyroid nodules, enlarged lymph nodes, and breast lumps.
otherNames: Xiao Li Wan (消疠丸)

allFormulas.name: Zi Yun Gao
allFormulas.summary: A classical topical ointment used for minor skin problems including burns, cuts, eczema, insect bites, cracked skin, and frostbite. It cools inflamed skin, promotes tissue repair, and moisturizes dry or damaged areas. Made from just a few natural ingredients infused in sesame oil, it has been a household skin remedy in East Asia for over 400 years.
categories: Topical formulas for sores and wounds
tcmActions: Clears Heat and cools the Blood
otherNames: Run Ji Gao (润肌膏, Flesh-Moistening Ointment)
Zi Cao Gao (紫草膏, Lithospermum Ointment)
Shiunko (紫云膏, Japanese Kampo name)

allFormulas.name: San Jin Wan
allFormulas.summary: A widely used Chinese herbal formula for urinary tract health, designed to clear heat and dampness from the bladder while supporting kidney function. It is commonly taken for symptoms like burning or painful urination, urinary urgency and frequency, and dark or cloudy urine associated with urinary tract infections, cystitis, and chronic prostatitis.
tcmActions: Promotes urination and unblocks Lin syndrome
Drains Dampness from the lower burner
allFormulas.dynasty: Modern era (contemporary Chinese patent medicine, 20th century)
otherNames: San Jin Pian (三金片, Triple Gold Tablets)

allFormulas.name: Xiao Jin Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Qing dynasty used to dissolve stubborn lumps, nodules, and masses caused by the combination of Cold, Phlegm, and stagnant Blood congealing in the body's tissues. It is commonly used for breast lumps, thyroid nodules, lymph node swelling, and similar conditions where firm, painfully hard masses develop under the skin without redness or heat. The formula works by warming the channels, breaking up Phlegm, and restoring Blood circulation to the affected area.
tcmActions: Warms the channels and opens the collaterals
otherNames: Xiao Jin Dan (小金丹, Minor Golden Elixir)

allFormulas.name: An Chong Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula designed for women experiencing prolonged or excessive menstrual bleeding caused by underlying weakness. It works by strengthening the body's ability to hold Blood in its proper channels, stabilizing the uterus, and replenishing lost Blood and nutrients. It is best suited for chronic, moderate bleeding rather than acute heavy hemorrhage.
tcmActions: Tonifies Qi and strengthens the Spleen
allFormulas.dynasty: Late Qing dynasty to early Republic period, first published 1918–1934 CE

allFormulas.name: Bai He Zhi Mu Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for lily disease (bǎi hé bìng) after sweating, used to nourish Yin, clear deficiency heat and calm the mind. It helps with restlessness, palpitations, dry cough, insomnia and irritability that arise when body fluids are depleted.
tcmActions: Clears heat and calms the spirit
Moistens the Lungs and stops cough
Tonifies the Heart and relieves irritability

allFormulas.name: Bai Ye Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Jin Gui Yao Lue that warms the middle jiao and stops bleeding, used for vomiting blood, nosebleeds or coughing up blood due to deficiency cold of the Spleen and Stomach.
tcmActions: Warms the channels and stops bleeding
Warms the middle and dispels cold to stop bleeding

allFormulas.name: Zhi Zhu Wan
allFormulas.englishName: Immature Bitter Orange and Atractylodes Pill
allFormulas.summary: Zhi Zhu Wan is a traditional Chinese formula used to strengthen weak digestion, relieve bloating, and improve appetite. It combines Atractylodes to tonify Spleen Qi and immature bitter orange to move Qi and eliminate stagnation. It is commonly used for symptoms like epigastric fullness, poor appetite, and fatigue due to digestive weakness.

allFormulas.name: Da Xian Xiong Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Shang Han Lun used to drain heat and expel water from the chest, addressing severe chest and epigastric hardness, pain, neck stiffness, and constipation caused by heat and water binding in the chest.
tcmActions: Purges Heat and unblocks the bowels
otherNames: Xiàn Xiōng Wán (陷胸丸, Sinking into the Chest Pill)

allFormulas.name: Chang Shan Yin
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula used to interrupt malaria attacks. It directly targets the malarial pathogen, breaks the cycle of chills and fever, and helps control severe nausea and vomiting that often accompany the condition, while protecting the body's fluids.
tcmActions: Harmonizes the stomach and stops vomiting
otherNames: Héng Shān Yǐn (恒山饮, Dichroa Drink)

allFormulas.name: Liang Xue Di Huang Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical decoction used to cool the Blood and stop bleeding caused by Heat, especially useful for hemorrhoids, anal bleeding, and other conditions where Heat in the Blood leads to reckless bleeding. It clears Damp-Heat from the Lower Burner and relieves pain and swelling.
categories: Formula that cool the Blood and stop bleeding

allFormulas.name: Zhi Shi Shao Yao Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Immature Bitter Orange and Peony Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A succinct classical formula of just two herbs that works to gently but effectively break through stagnant Qi and soothe abdominal pain, especially after childbirth. It is valued for its ability to relieve distending, oppressive pain without harshly disturbing the postpartum body, combining an herb that moves Qi with one that nourishes and calms the Blood.
otherNames: Zhi Shi Shao Yao San (枳实芍药散, Immature Bitter Orange and Peony Powder)

allFormulas.name: Xiang Lian Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical two-herb pill that clears Heat and Dampness from the intestines while moving Qi to relieve abdominal pain and tenesmus. It is most commonly used for acute diarrhea or dysentery with cramping, urgency, and a sensation of incomplete evacuation.
categories: Formulas that clear Heat and expel dampness

allFormulas.name: Wu Shen Tang
allFormulas.summary: A modern clinical formula used to strengthen the energy and fluids of the heart while clearing viral heat toxins. It is especially employed for supporting recovery from viral myocarditis, addressing fatigue, palpitations, chest discomfort, and breathlessness.

allFormulas.name: Er Mu San
allFormulas.summary: A simple two-herb classical formula that clears Heat from the Lungs, dissolves sticky phlegm, and moistens dryness. It is used for persistent cough with thick yellow phlegm, dry throat, or chronic cough caused by Lung Heat that has begun to deplete the body's internal moisture. Particularly suited for people whose cough worsens with warming remedies.
categories: Formulas that clear Heat and transform Phlegm
tcmActions: Moistens the Lungs and stops coughing
Nourishes Yin and clears deficiency Heat
allFormulas.dynasty: The Ji Jiu Xian Fang dates to approximately the Yuán dynasty (~14th century CE); the formula was further elaborated by Wang Ang in the Qīng dynasty (1682 CE)

allFormulas.name: Sheng Xian Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula that tonifies Qi and lifts sunken Qi, used for shortness of breath, chest oppression, and fatigue caused by sinking of the chest Qi.

allFormulas.name: Zhu Jing Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classical three-herb pill that strengthens the Liver and Kidneys, nourishes the blood and essence, and sharpens eyesight. It is traditionally used for declining vision, blurry sight, floaters, and dark shadows in front of the eyes caused by deficiency of the Liver and Kidneys.
tcmActions: Brightens the eyes and improves vision

allFormulas.name: Hua Gai San
allFormulas.summary: Hua Gai San is a traditional Chinese herbal formula used to relieve cough, wheezing, and chest congestion caused by a common cold or respiratory infection. It works by dispersing wind-cold and clearing phlegm from the lungs.
tcmActions: Disperses the Lungs and releases the exterior
otherNames: Huá Gài Tāng (华盖汤, Canopy Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Ju Pi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classic 2-herb formula from the Jin Gui Yao Lue that quickly warms the stomach, dispels Cold, and stops hiccup and nausea caused by Cold invading the stomach. It is especially useful for sudden hiccups accompanied by cold hands and feet.
tcmActions: Regulates Qi and Harmonizes the Stomach
otherNames: Shēng Jiāng Jú Pí Tāng (生姜橘皮汤, Fresh Ginger and Tangerine Peel Decoction)
Xiǎo Jú Pí Tāng (小橘皮汤, Minor Tangerine Peel Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Gui Zhi Qu Shao Yao Jia Fu Zi Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Cinnamon Twig Decoction Minus Peony Plus Aconite
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Shang Han Lun used to treat lingering cold after a mistaken purgative. It warms the chest, restores depleted Yang, and gently releases lingering Wind-Cold. Patients often present with a feeling of fullness or pressure in the chest, a rapid or irregular pulse, and a slight aversion to cold.
tcmActions: Releases the exterior and dispels Wind
Harmonizes the protective and nutritive Qi

allFormulas.name: Zhi Shi Xie Bai Gui Zhi Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Immature Bitter Orange, Chinese Chive, and Cinnamon Twig Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Jin Gui Yao Lue used to treat chest pain, stuffiness, and shortness of breath caused by weakness of chest yang and accumulation of phlegm. It warms and unblocks the chest, dissolves phlegm, and moves stagnant qi to relieve discomfort.
categories: Formulas that treat chest painful obstruction (Xiong Bi)
tcmActions: Descends qi and opens the chest

allFormulas.name: Fang Feng Jie Du Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula used to release wind-heat, clear internal toxins, and promote the eruption of rashes such as measles. It is especially suited for warm-season exanthematous diseases where fever and skin rash are prominent.
otherNames: Fang Feng Bai Du San (防风败毒散, Fangfeng Detoxifying Powder)

allFormulas.name: Huang Lian Gao
allFormulas.summary: A classic Chinese herbal ointment that cools Heat, dries oozing and itching, and soothes painful, inflamed skin. It is used topically on eczema, burns, boils, acne and other hot, red, swollen skin conditions, helping to reduce inflammation and speed the healing of damaged tissue.
categories: Topical formulas for sores and wounds
tcmActions: Cools the Blood and moistens Dryness
Promotes tissue regeneration and heals wounds

allFormulas.name: Jian Ling Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from Zhang Xichun’s “Records of Chinese Medicine with Reference to Western Medicine” that soothes the Liver, extinguishes Wind, nourishes Yin, and calms the mind. It is primarily used for high blood pressure, dizziness, throbbing headaches, tinnitus, irritability, and insomnia caused by Liver Yang rising with an underlying Yin deficiency.
categories: Soothes the Liver and removes the Liver Stagnation
tcmActions: Soothes the Liver and extinguishes Wind
Nourishes Yin and calms the Mind

allFormulas.name: Xi Xian San
allFormulas.summary: Xi Xian Powder is a traditional Chinese herbal formula made from the single herb Xi Xian Cao (Siegesbeckia). It is used to relieve joint and muscle pain caused by Wind-Dampness and Damp-Heat, such as in rheumatoid arthritis, gout, or fibromyalgia. When processed, it also supports the Liver and Kidney, helping with chronic lower back and knee weakness.

allFormulas.name: Fu Ling Gui Zhi Gan Cao Da Zao Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Poria, Cinnamon Twig, Licorice, and Jujube Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Shang Han Lun designed for people who experience a distinctive throbbing or fluttering sensation below the navel, often with anxiety and a feeling of something surging upward from the abdomen toward the chest. It works by warming the Heart, strengthening digestion, and helping the body drain excess fluid accumulation from the lower abdomen through urination.
categories: Formulas that warm and transform water and Dampness
tcmActions: Calms the Qi and subdues surging
Strengthens the Spleen to control Water
allFormulas.dynasty: Eastern Han dynasty (东汉), circa 200 CE
otherNames: Líng Guì Zǎo Gān Tāng (苓桂枣甘汤)

allFormulas.name: Ma Huang Fu Zi Xi Xin Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula from the Shang Han Lun designed for people who catch a cold when their body is already weakened, particularly when they feel extremely cold, deeply tired, and have a weak pulse. It works by warming the body's core while gently helping it expel the cold from the surface. It is also widely used in modern practice for conditions like allergic rhinitis, slow heart rate, and cold-type joint pain when the underlying pattern involves Yang deficiency.
categories: Formulas that clear Exterior disorders with Interior deficiency
tcmActions: Assists Yang and releases the exterior
Warms the channels and disperses Cold
otherNames: Ma Huang Xi Xin Fu Zi Tang (麻黄细辛附子汤)

allFormulas.name: Niu Huang Shang Qing Wan
allFormulas.englishName: Niu Huang Shang Qing Wan (Cow Bezoar Upper-Heat-Clearing Pill)
allFormulas.summary: A classic modern pill that relieves intense upper‑body Heat symptoms such as sore throat, red eyes, mouth sores and headache, by clearing internal Fire and dispersing Wind‑Heat.
categories: Formulas that clear Heat and resolve toxicity

allFormulas.name: Qing Fei Yin
allFormulas.summary: Qing Fei Yin is a classical TCM formula that clears Heat from the Lungs, relieves cough and thirst, and promotes urination. It is used for conditions like acute bronchitis or urinary tract infections when symptoms include cough with yellow phlegm, dry mouth, and difficult urination.
allFormulas.dynasty: Jin Dynasty (1115–1234), attributed to Li Dongyuan (Li Gao)
otherNames: Dongyuan Qing Fei Yin (东垣清肺饮, Dongyuan Lung-Clearing Drink)

allFormulas.name: Dang Gui San
allFormulas.summary: A traditional Chinese herbal formula from the Jin Gui Yao Lue (Essential Prescriptions of the Golden Cabinet), used during pregnancy to nourish blood, clear heat, and prevent miscarriage. It is commonly taken to support a healthy pregnancy, especially for women with a history of miscarriage or symptoms of vaginal bleeding and abdominal pain.
otherNames: An Tai Wan (安胎丸, Fetus-Calming Pill)
Wu Wei An Tai Wan (五味安胎丸, Five-Ingredient Fetus-Calming Pill)
Shao Yao Tang (芍药汤, Peony Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Ren Shen Hu Tao Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical tonic formula used to strengthen the Lungs and Kidneys for people suffering from chronic cough, wheezing, and shortness of breath that worsens with activity. It helps the body breathe more deeply and reduces reliance on inhalers, especially in elderly individuals with weak, lingering respiratory conditions.
otherNames: Guanyin Ren Shen Hu Tao Tang (观音人参胡桃汤, Guanyin Ginseng and Walnut Decoction)

allFormulas.name: Dan Dao Pai Shi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A modern formula for clearing Damp-Heat from the Liver and Gallbladder, moving Qi to relieve pain, and promoting bile flow to expel gallstones. It is used for acute cholecystitis, biliary colic, common bile duct stones, and residual stones after surgery.
tcmActions: Promotes bile flow and expels stones

allFormulas.name: Huang Qi Fu Zi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula that warms yang and promotes urination to reduce edema, especially water retention due to deficiency of Spleen and Kidney yang. It is commonly used for puffiness, swelling of the limbs, and sensations of cold in the body.

allFormulas.name: Sheng Ji San
allFormulas.summary: A classical external powder used to heal chronic ulcers, wounds, and sores that refuse to close. It clears lingering infection, breaks stagnant Blood, dries excess moisture, and stimulates the growth of healthy new skin. Applied directly to the wound, it helps transform a slow-healing lesion into one that actively regenerates.
categories: Topical formulas for sores and wounds
tcmActions: Expels putrid flesh and generates new tissue

allFormulas.name: Wu Mo Yin Zi
allFormulas.summary: A classical emergency formula designed to powerfully restore the smooth flow of Qi when it becomes severely blocked, typically after intense anger or emotional shock. It uses five aromatic herbs ground with wine to rapidly break through Qi stagnation, relieve chest and abdominal distension, ease breathing difficulty, and revive consciousness in cases of Qi-related fainting. In modern practice, it is also used for severe bloating, intestinal paralysis, and stress-related digestive complaints.
tcmActions: Promotes Qi movement and resolves stagnation
Resolves Qi constraint from emotional upset
otherNames: Wu Mo Yin (五磨饮)

allFormulas.name: Liu Mo Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula that strongly moves Qi, clears heat, and unblocks the bowels. It is used for conditions where stress and emotional tension cause the digestive Qi to become stuck, leading to abdominal bloating, pain, and severe constipation with a sense of heat. By restoring the downward movement of Qi, Liu Mo Tang relieves pressure in the abdomen and helps normal bowel function return.
otherNames: Liu Mo Yin Zi (六磨饮子, Six Milled-Herb Drink)

allFormulas.name: Hu Wei Cheng Qi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A gentle purgative formula from the Warm Disease school that clears residual Heat from the Stomach and Intestines while nourishing Yin to protect the Stomach. It is used for constipation, dry mouth, and thirst that occur after a feverish illness, when Heat has damaged the body's fluids.

allFormulas.name: Qu Tao Tang
allFormulas.summary: Qu Tao Tang is a specialized formula for expelling intestinal tapeworms. It combines purgative, Qi-moving, and heat-clearing herbs to flush out parasites and relieve abdominal discomfort, distension, and digestive upset caused by taeniasis.

allFormulas.name: Liang Xue Qing Fei Yin
allFormulas.englishName: Cool the Blood and Clear the Lung Drink
allFormulas.summary: A modern clinical formula that cools the Blood and clears Heat from the Lungs and Stomach to treat stubborn facial skin conditions like acne, rosacea, and seborrheic dermatitis.

allFormulas.name: Yang Xue Ding Feng Tang
allFormulas.englishName: Nourish the Blood and Calm the Wind Decoction
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for persistent, widespread itching without visible rash or sores. It works by deeply nourishing the Blood and Yin (the body's moistening reserves), which addresses the underlying dryness that causes the skin to itch. Originally recorded in the Complete Book of Surgical Patterns and Treatments, it is particularly suited for older adults or anyone whose itching worsens in dry weather or at night.

allFormulas.name: Zhu Ye Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classic heat-clearing formula from the Tang dynasty, used for intense thirst, dry mouth, and irritability caused by strong Stomach heat. It cools internal fire, generates body fluids, and calms the mind.

allFormulas.name: Zhi Zi Bo Pi Tang
allFormulas.summary: A classical formula for damp-heat jaundice with heat predominating, used to reduce yellowing of the skin and eyes, relieve fever, and clear dark urine by draining damp-heat from the Liver and Gallbladder.
categories: Formulas that clear Heat and expel dampness
otherNames: Bo Pi Tang (柏皮汤, Phellodendron Bark Decoction)
Bo Pi San (柏皮散, Phellodendron Bark Powder)

allFormulas.name: Zhu Che Wan
allFormulas.summary: A classic Chinese herbal pill that helps stop chronic diarrhea or dysentery with bloody stools, especially when long-lasting intestinal heat has damaged the body's fluids and blood. It works by clearing lingering heat, nourishing yin and blood, and gently warming the digestive system to restore balance.
tcmActions: Secures the intestines and stops dysentery

allFormulas.name: An Mian Tang
allFormulas.summary:
An Mian Tang is a concise six-herb formula designed to promote restful sleep by nourishing Heart Blood, calming the spirit (Shen), clearing irritability arising from depressive Heat, and harmonizing the Stomach. 

It is suited for individuals whose insomnia stems from a combination of Blood deficiency failing to anchor the spirit, mild internal Heat generating restlessness, and digestive disharmony that unsettles sleep. 

Compared to larger sedative formulas, An Mian Tang takes a balanced, moderate approach—gentle enough for extended use yet effective enough to address the intertwined emotional, thermal, and digestive roots of poor sleep.
tcmActions: Nourishes Blood and calms the spirit
Harmonizes the Stomach and dissolves food stagnation
otherNames: Calm Sleep Decoction
